basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 2.' and it opens 'Vers. 2. Accusavit fratres suos apud patrem crimine pessimo. Putant quidam quod'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 2. Accusavit fratres suos apud patrem crimine pessimo. Putant quidam quod accusaverit eos quia cum pecoribus commiscebantur. Sic Alwinus in Quaestionibus suis. Alii dicunt quod Ruben pro concubina patris solum accusaverit. Quod si ita est, per synecdochen, id est a toto partem debemus accipere. | Non enim omnes fratres accusavit, sed unum solum.
